correctness.rationale: The frozen seven-file package and current main directory have the same seven Git blob IDs; constructing the Git tree from actual sorted 100644 entries reproduces def2ce0baeb2eddc05b335d36b7c2e4d373296bd. For each smooth radial graph r_epsilon(omega)=1+epsilon phi(omega), the area density differentiates to 2 phi d omega. Differentiating the fixed signed-height slab indicator contributes t phi delta(t-s) and -t phi delta(t-s-h), because -1<s<s+h<1 gives transverse boundary circles. Applying Funk--Hecke with P_l(1)=1 and surface area measure 4pi yields 2pi times [2 integral_s^{s+h}P_l(t)dt+s P_l(s)-(s+h)P_l(s+h)], equal by integration by parts to 2pi J_l(s,h), J_l=integral_s^{s+h}(P_l-tP_l')dt. For l=0 J_0=h; l=1 J_1=0. For l>=2, P_l(t) has leading coefficient c_l=(2l)!/[2^l(l!)^2], so J_l as a polynomial in s has leading coefficient h(1-l)c_l !=0 and degree l. Each exceptional zero set is finite; all degrees union countable, so outside it harmonic projections l>=2 are forced zero, with H_1 the exact translation kernel. The same polynomial argument handles any nonempty open interval of offsets; odd Legendre parity annihilates all odd degrees at centered s=-h/2. A separately written exact symbolic calculation checked the integral/boundary identities, nonzero leading coefficients and parity through l=9, and independent direct radial-area finite differences for zonal l=0..4 at h=.73,s=-.39 agreed with 2pi J_l to better than 1e-10. These checks only corroborate the analytic infinite-degree proof, and no unproved nonlinear inverse or stability statement is inferred.
residual_risks: No uniform lower bound on nonzero |J_l| or stable inverse; smooth injectivity alone can be very ill conditioned.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality PASS for the exact one-absolute-height linearized measurement kernel, generic-in-offset injectivity modulo translations, and infinitely many centered odd blind modes. The complete lawful public full text of Lai's earlier arXiv:2610.01550v1, accessible via ResearchGate's CC BY full-text presentation, was materially read across the theorem, convexity argument, coarea-periodicity, periodic-wave method, elementary width lemma and appendix. It proves nonlinear sphere characterization under all translated width-h slabs, not an infinitesimal single-offset spectrum. The revised Ghomi--Howard--Lai full 17-page author-hosted manuscript likewise proves nonlinear rigidity using all offsets, periodic height densities, potential averaging and microlocal arguments; it supplies no shape derivative, Legendre multiplier or kernel at one fixed signed height. These two global theorems do not imply injectivity of the differential of a strictly weaker single-offset data operator. Standard Funk--Hecke is acknowledged; obtaining the particular boundary-weighted kernel and proving nonzero polynomial eigenvalues in every degree are the submitted mathematical steps. Fresh independent published Resultary semantic searches found the exact submitted entry and mathematically different spherical-spectrum, Radon and rigidity findings, not a separate covering predecessor. The near-contemporary source set and preexisting harmonic-transform techniques are recorded as priority/implicit-corollary risks, not a guarantee of historical priority.
residual_risks: The formula is obtained by a short first-variation plus classical Funk--Hecke argument, so one could treat it as an implicit but not stated consequence of existing spherical-convolution machinery; historical novelty is best-of-knowledge only.
An older geometric-tomography paper may have the same shape-derivative or kernel under terminology outside the queries; no universal literature-completeness claim.
The metric-space inverse may be ill-conditioned because nonzero Legendre multipliers can be small; no stability/noise theorem is asserted.

value.rationale: This is a natural structural measurement-kernel question arising immediately from the recently studied fixed-width Archimedean sphere problem. A geometric observer may acquire every normal direction at only one absolute position; identifying precisely when those measurements distinguish infinitesimal shapes (up to unavoidable translational motions) is useful even without nonlinear inversion. The theorem gives the complete per-offset kernel, an all-degree countable exceptional set with at most l roots for degree l, and a qualitative sensor-placement dichotomy: a generic offset detects all shape modes, whereas the geometrically natural centered offset misses the infinite-dimensional odd subspace. The boundary-motion term distinguishes the physical surface-area derivative from textbook fixed-domain spherical convolution. It is a modest but motivated exact inverse-geometric structural classification, not just a named formula, a routine parameter substitution, an arbitrary low-mode check, or a stability claim. Its narrow scope (one round sphere, smooth deformations, first order only, implicitly described exceptional set) is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Novelty/value are focused on exact one-offset identifiability and centered information loss, not a general tomography inversion or constructive stable estimator.
The proof uses classical tools in a short computation; contribution is specialized rather than a broad new method.

limitations: Strictly infinitesimal operator at the centered unit sphere and fixed signed heights; not nonlinear one-offset recovery.
No uniform stability, quantitative small-singular-value bound or fully enumerated exceptional offsets.
Generic one-offset statement quantifies over all directions u for each fixed s, not just one measured direction.
